content.title: Submit an over-limit order from review into a pending approval request
content.test_md_blob:
# Submit an over-limit order from review into a pending approval request

> Prove that approval routing uses the final order total including tax and delivery, shows the over-limit review state, and creates a pending approval request when the buyer submits.

## Step 1

Open {{start_url}} in a browser, sign in to the NovaTech Business Store as a Buyer with {{buyer_login}} and {{buyer_password}}, and open the prepared quote {{over_limit_quote_locator}} so its order review page is displayed.

## Step 2 @verifies ac-17, ac-18, ac-19

On the order review page for {{over_limit_quote_locator}}, in the payment method section ensure Purchase Order is selected and enter {{valid_po_number}}, then assert the over-limit banner reads "This order exceeds the $25,000 spending limit and requires Procurement Manager approval.", the primary action reads "Submit for Approval", and the displayed order total including tax and delivery is greater than $25,000.

## Step 3 @verifies ac-20, ac-21, ac-22, ac-23, ac-24

From the same order review page, submit the request for approval and wait for the resulting approval request view, then assert a request ID matching REQ-##### is shown with status "Pending Approval", the requester's name is shown, the order total is shown, and the submitted time is shown.

  - objective: On the order review page for {{over_limit_quote_locator}}, in the payment method section ensure Purchase Order is selected and enter {{valid_po_number}}, then assert the over-limit banner reads "This order exceeds the $25,000 spending limit and requires Procurement Manager approval.", the primary action reads "Submit for Approval", and the displayed order total including tax and delivery is greater than $25,000.

# Place an order totaling exactly $25,000 directly without approval

> Prove that the spending rule is strict: an order at exactly $25,000 does not require approval and does not enter the approval path.

## Step 1

Open {{start_url}} in a browser, sign in to the NovaTech Business Store as a Buyer with {{buyer_login}} and {{buyer_password}}, and open the prepared quote {{exact_limit_quote_locator}} so its order review page is displayed.

## Step 2 @verifies ac-25

On the order review page for {{exact_limit_quote_locator}}, in the payment method section ensure Purchase Order is selected and enter {{valid_po_number}} if needed, then store the current review state as baseline_direct_place_review and assert the displayed order total including tax and delivery equals $25,000 and the primary action reads "Place Order".

## Step 3 @verifies ac-25

From that review state, place the order, then assert the flow goes directly to the order confirmation page without any approval-request step and the confirmation shows an order number beginning with NT-.

title: Place an order totaling exactly $25,000 directly without approval

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Scored highest because this path carried the core authorization control: if it fails, an over-limit purchase can bypass approval or fail to create a traceable approval request.
[value_score] Scored second because the exact-threshold boundary is the strongest single guard against off-by-one misrouting at the spending limit.

[self_critique] The written check anchored on ac-21 because 'Pending Approval' is the clearest pass/fail oracle for successful approval submission. The scenario technique fit the happy approval path, the complementary non-approval case was covered by t2, and the final assert stayed limited to the source-promised approval-request artifacts rather than unrelated approval-page behavior.

[self_critique] The written check used a state-transition oracle from the exact-threshold review state into direct placement, which directly proved ac-25. The boundary technique fit the off-by-one risk, the negative absence of approval was embedded in the confirmation-path assert, and the final assert stayed focused on direct placement rather than broader confirmation-page details.
